axe-core Rule: image-alt, aria-meter-name, aria-progressbar-name, input-image-alt, role-img-alt, svg-img-alt, object-alt
automated checks (axe core rules ): Images have alternative text where required (non-decorative images).
Decorative images are marked with empty alternative text (alt="") or implemented as CSS backgrounds.
Inputs have appropriate accessible names.
Embedded multimedia is identified using accessible text alternatives.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Linked images have descriptive and meaningful alternative text.
Equivalent text alternatives for complex images are provided in context or via a separate linked page.
Form buttons have descriptive values that convey their purpose.
Frames and iframes have appropriate and descriptive titles.
Total conditions: Images have alternative text where required (non-decorative images).
Decorative images are marked with empty alternative text (alt="") or implemented as CSS backgrounds.
Linked images have descriptive and meaningful alternative text.
Equivalent text alternatives for complex images are provided in context or via a separate linked page.
Form buttons have descriptive values that convey their purpose.
Inputs have appropriate accessible names.
Embedded multimedia is identified using accessible text alternatives.
Frames and iframes have appropriate and descriptive titles.
webaim checks:
1.Images, image buttons, and image map hot spots have appropriate, equivalent alternative text.
 2.Images that do not convey content, are decorative, or contain content that is already conveyed in text are given empty
alternative text (alt="") or implemented as CSS backgrounds. 
3.All linked images have descriptive alternative text.
 Equivalent alternatives to complex images are provided in context or on a separate linked page.
 4.Form buttons have a descriptive value.
5. Inputs have appropriate accessible names.
6. Embedded multimedia is identified via accessible text.
 7.Frames and iframes are appropriately titled.

Remaining conditions required for full S: Audio-only media elements include a mechanism (such as a track or accessible reference) indicating the presence of a transcript or caption alternative.
A complete and accurate transcript is provided for all non-live audio-only content.
The transcript includes all relevant spoken dialogue and meaningful sounds.
For non-live video-only content, a descriptive transcript or audio description is provided.
Decorative video-only content is correctly identified and does not require a transcript.
Transcripts or audio descriptions are easy to locate and accessible to users.
The transcript or audio description accurately reflects the timing and meaning of the media content.
Total conditions: Audio-only media elements include a mechanism (such as a track or accessible reference) indicating the presence of a transcript or caption alternative.
A complete and accurate transcript is provided for all non-live audio-only content.
The transcript includes all relevant spoken dialogue and meaningful sounds.
For non-live video-only content, a descriptive transcript or audio description is provided.
Decorative video-only content is correctly identified and does not require a transcript.
Transcripts or audio descriptions are easy to locate and accessible to users.
The transcript or audio description accurately reflects the timing and meaning of the media content.
webaim checks:
1.A descriptive transcript of relevant content is provided for non-live audio-only (audio podcasts, MP3 files, etc.).
2. A descriptive transcript or audio description of relevant content is provided for non-live video-only, unless the video
is decorative.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Prerecorded video elements include a captions track (<track kind="captions">) associated with the video.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Captions are synchronized accurately with the audio.
Captions include all spoken dialogue and relevant non-speech audio (e.g., sound effects).
Captions are complete for the entire duration of the prerecorded video.
Total conditions: Prerecorded video elements include a captions track (<track kind="captions">) associated with the video.
Captions are synchronized accurately with the audio.
Captions include all spoken dialogue and relevant non-speech audio (e.g., sound effects).
Captions are complete for the entire duration of the prerecorded video.
webaim checks: Synchronized captions are provided for non-live video (YouTube videos, etc.).

Remaining conditions required for full S: A descriptive transcript or audio description is provided for non-live video.NOTE: Only required if there is relevant visual content that is not presented in the audio.
Total conditions: A descriptive transcript or audio description is provided for non-live video.NOTE: Only required if there is relevant visual content that is not presented in the audio.
webaim checks:
A descriptive transcript or audio description is provided for non-live video.
NOTE: Only required if there is relevant visual content that is not presented in the audio.

Remaining conditions required for full S: Synchronized captions are provided for live media that contains audio (audio-only broadcasts, web casts, video conferences, etc.)
Total conditions: Synchronized captions are provided for live media that contains audio (audio-only broadcasts, web casts, video conferences, etc.)
webaim checks: Synchronized captions are provided for live media that contains audio (audio-only broadcasts, web casts, video conferences, etc.)

Total conditions: A sign language video is provided for media that contains audio

Remaining conditions required for full S: When audio description cannot be added to video due to insufficient pauses in the audio, an alternative version of the video with pauses that allow audio descriptions is provided.
Total conditions: When audio description cannot be added to video due to insufficient pauses in the audio, an alternative version of the video with pauses that allow audio descriptions is provided.

Remaining conditions required for full S: A descriptive transcript is provided for pre-recorded media that has a video track.

axe-core Rule: aria-required-children, aria-required-parent, list, dlitem, listitem, th-has-data-cells
automated checks (axe core rules ): ARIA parent roles that require specific child roles contain all required child elements (for example, role="list" contains role="listitem").
Headings, landmarks, lists, and other structural elements are marked up using correct native HTML semantics.
Lists are implemented using appropriate HTML elements (ul, ol, dl) or correct ARIA roles where HTML is insufficient.
Data table headers are correctly associated with their corresponding data cells.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Tables are used only for tabular data and not for layout purposes.
Data tables include captions when needed and captions are correctly associated with the tables.
Form inputs have visible and programmatically associated text labels.
Related form controls are grouped using fieldset and legend where appropriate.
ARIA labelling is used correctly only when native HTML semantics are insufficient.
Total conditions: ARIA parent roles that require specific child roles contain all required child elements (for example, role="list" contains role="listitem").
Headings, landmarks, lists, and other structural elements are marked up using correct native HTML semantics.
Lists are implemented using appropriate HTML elements (ul, ol, dl) or correct ARIA roles where HTML is insufficient.
Tables are used only for tabular data and not for layout purposes.
Data table headers are correctly associated with their corresponding data cells.
Data tables include captions when needed and captions are correctly associated with the tables.
Form inputs have visible and programmatically associated text labels.
Related form controls are grouped using fieldset and legend where appropriate.
ARIA labelling is used correctly only when native HTML semantics are insufficient.
webaim checks:
1.Semantic markup is appropriately used to designate headings, regions/landmarks, lists, emphasized or special text,
etc.
 2.Tables are used for tabular data and data cells are associated with their headers. Data table captions, if present, are
associated to data tables.
3. Text labels are associated with form inputs. Related form controls are grouped with fieldset/legend. ARIA labelling
may be used when standard HTML is insufficient.

Remaining conditions required for full S: The reading and navigation order (determined by code order) is logical and intuitive
Total conditions: The reading and navigation order (determined by code order) is logical and intuitive
webaim checks: The reading and navigation order (determined by code order) is logical and intuitive

Remaining conditions required for full S: Instructions do not rely upon shape, size, or visual location (e.g., "Click the square icon to continue" or "Instructions are in the right-hand column").
Instructions do not rely upon sound (e.g., "A beeping sound indicates you may continue.")
Total conditions: Instructions do not rely upon shape, size, or visual location (e.g., "Click the square icon to continue" or "Instructions are in the right-hand column").
Instructions do not rely upon sound (e.g., "A beeping sound indicates you may continue.")
webaim checks:

 Instructions do not rely upon sound (e.g., "A beeping sound indicates you may continue.")

Remaining conditions required for full S: Orientation of web content is not restricted to only portrait or landscape, unless a specific orientation is necessary.
Total conditions: Orientation of web content is not restricted to only portrait or landscape, unless a specific orientation is necessary.
webaim checks: Orientation of web content is not restricted to only portrait or landscape, unless a specific orientation is necessary.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Form input fields that support autocomplete use valid and appropriate autocomplete attribute values as defined by the HTML specification.
Remaining conditions required for full S: The selected autocomplete values accurately reflect the intended purpose of each input field (e.g., name, email, address).
Autocomplete attributes are applied to all relevant user data fields where applicable.
Inputs that should not have autocomplete do not include inappropriate autocomplete values.
Total conditions: Form input fields that support autocomplete use valid and appropriate autocomplete attribute values as defined by the HTML specification.
The selected autocomplete values accurately reflect the intended purpose of each input field (e.g., name, email, address).
Autocomplete attributes are applied to all relevant user data fields where applicable.
Inputs that should not have autocomplete do not include inappropriate autocomplete values.
webaim checks:
Input fields that collect certain types of user information have an
 appropriate autocomplete attribute defined

Remaining conditions required for full S: Regions/landmarks are used to identify page regions.
ARIA is used, where appropriate, to enhance HTML semantics to better identify the purpose of interface components.
Total conditions: Regions/landmarks are used to identify page regions.
ARIA is used, where appropriate, to enhance HTML semantics to better identify the purpose of interface components.
webaim checks:

ARIA is used, where appropriate, to enhance HTML semantics to better identify the purpose of interface

automated checks (axe core rules ): Links within blocks of text are visually distinguishable from surrounding text without relying on color alone.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Color is not used as the sole method to convey information, indicate status, prompt action, or distinguish visual elements other than links.
Non-link visual cues (icons, charts, error messages, required fields, instructions) do not rely on color alone.
The contrast ratio between link text and surrounding text is at least 3:1 when color is used to distinguish links.
Links provide an additional visual indicator (such as underline) on hover and keyboard focus.
Visual distinctions conveyed by color are also available programmatically or through text alternatives.
Total conditions: Links within blocks of text are visually distinguishable from surrounding text without relying on color alone.
Color is not used as the sole method to convey information, indicate status, prompt action, or distinguish visual elements other than links.
Non-link visual cues (icons, charts, error messages, required fields, instructions) do not rely on color alone.
The contrast ratio between link text and surrounding text is at least 3:1 when color is used to distinguish links.
Links provide an additional visual indicator (such as underline) on hover and keyboard focus.
Visual distinctions conveyed by color are also available programmatically or through text alternatives.
webaim checks:
1. Color is not used as the sole method of conveying content or distinguishing visual elements.
2. Color alone is not used to distinguish links from surrounding text unless:
   a) The contrast ratio between the link and surrounding text is at least 3:1, AND
   b) An additional visual distinction (e.g., underline) is provided on hover and keyboard focus.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Audio does not automatically play for more than 3 seconds without a user-controlled mechanism to stop or pause it.
Remaining conditions required for full S: A visible and operable control is available to pause, stop, or mute the audio.
Audio controls are keyboard accessible.
Users can independently adjust audio volume without affecting system volume.
Audio control mechanisms are clearly labeled and understandable.
Total conditions: Audio does not automatically play for more than 3 seconds without a user-controlled mechanism to stop or pause it.
A visible and operable control is available to pause, stop, or mute the audio.
Audio controls are keyboard accessible.
Users can independently adjust audio volume without affecting system volume.
Audio control mechanisms are clearly labeled and understandable.
webaim checks:
A mechanism is provided to stop, pause, mute, or adjust volume for audio that automatically plays on a page for more
than 3 seconds.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Text and images of text meet the minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text.
Large-scale text meets the minimum contrast ratio of 3:1.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Text that is part of images is essential and cannot be presented using real text.
Contrast is evaluated correctly for text rendered over gradients, images, patterns, or videos.
Custom fonts, font weights, and font rendering do not reduce effective contrast below minimum thresholds.
Text contrast remains sufficient in all interaction states (hover, focus, active, visited).
Contrast is maintained when user styles, zoom, or high-contrast modes are applied.
Total conditions: Text and images of text meet the minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text.
Large-scale text meets the minimum contrast ratio of 3:1.
Text that is part of images is essential and cannot be presented using real text.
Contrast is evaluated correctly for text rendered over gradients, images, patterns, or videos.
Custom fonts, font weights, and font rendering do not reduce effective contrast below minimum thresholds.
Text contrast remains sufficient in all interaction states (hover, focus, active, visited).
Contrast is maintained when user styles, zoom, or high-contrast modes are applied.
webaim checks:
Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
 Large text - at least 18 point (typically 24px) or 14 point (typically 18.66px) and bold - has a contrast ratio of at least
3:1.

automated checks (axe core rules ): The viewport meta tag does not restrict user scaling (e.g., does not disable zoom or set maximum-scale less than 2).
Remaining conditions required for full S: Text content remains readable and does not become truncated, overlapped, or clipped when zoomed to 200%.
All functionality remains available and operable when the page is zoomed to 200%.
Horizontal scrolling is not required for reading blocks of text at 200% zoom (except where allowed).
Fixed-position or absolutely positioned content does not obscure text or controls when zoomed.
Interactive elements remain visible, usable, and discoverable at 200% zoom.
Total conditions: The viewport meta tag does not restrict user scaling (e.g., does not disable zoom or set maximum-scale less than 2).
Text content remains readable and does not become truncated, overlapped, or clipped when zoomed to 200%.
All functionality remains available and operable when the page is zoomed to 200%.
Horizontal scrolling is not required for reading blocks of text at 200% zoom (except where allowed).
Fixed-position or absolutely positioned content does not obscure text or controls when zoomed.
Interactive elements remain visible, usable, and discoverable at 200% zoom.
webaim checks:
The page is readable and functional when the page is zoomed to 200%.
NOTE: 1.4.10 (below) introduces additional requirements for zoomed content

Remaining conditions required for full S: If the same visual presentation can be made using text alone, an image is not used to present that text.
Total conditions: If the same visual presentation can be made using text alone, an image is not used to present that text.
webaim checks: If the same visual presentation can be made using text alone, an image is not used to present that text.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Text and images of text meet the enhanced minimum color contrast ratios of 7:1 for normal text and 4.5:1 for large or bold text based on computed foreground and background colors.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Contrast is sufficient in all user states, including hover, focus, active, disabled, and visited states.
Text displayed over images, gradients, patterns, or video maintains the required enhanced contrast ratios.
Contrast remains sufficient when custom user styles, zoom, or high-contrast modes are applied.
Images of text that contain meaningful content meet the enhanced contrast requirements.
Dynamically updated text content maintains enhanced contrast at all times.
Essential visual information conveyed through text is not lost due to insufficient contrast in real-world viewing conditions.
Total conditions: Text and images of text meet the enhanced minimum color contrast ratios of 7:1 for normal text and 4.5:1 for large or bold text based on computed foreground and background colors.
Contrast is sufficient in all user states, including hover, focus, active, disabled, and visited states.
Text displayed over images, gradients, patterns, or video maintains the required enhanced contrast ratios.
Contrast remains sufficient when custom user styles, zoom, or high-contrast modes are applied.
Images of text that contain meaningful content meet the enhanced contrast requirements.
Dynamically updated text content maintains enhanced contrast at all times.
Essential visual information conveyed through text is not lost due to insufficient contrast in real-world viewing conditions.
webaim checks:
Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 7:1.
 Large text - at least 18 point (typically 24px) or 14 point (typically 18.66px) and bold - has a contrast ratio of at least
4.5:1.

Remaining conditions required for full S: Audio with speech has no or very low background noise so the speech is easily distinguished.
Total conditions: Audio with speech has no or very low background noise so the speech is easily distinguished.
webaim checks: Audio with speech has no or very low background noise so the speech is easily distinguished.

Remaining conditions required for full S: Blocks of text over one sentence in length:
o Are no more than 80 characters wide.
o Are NOT fully justified (aligned to both the left and the right margins).
o Have adequate line spacing (at least 1/2 the height of the text) and paragraph spacing (1.5 times line spacing).
o Have defined or inherited foreground and background colors.
o Do NOT require horizontal scrolling when the text size is doubled.
Total conditions: Blocks of text over one sentence in length:
o Are no more than 80 characters wide.
o Are NOT fully justified (aligned to both the left and the right margins).
o Have adequate line spacing (at least 1/2 the height of the text) and paragraph spacing (1.5 times line spacing).
o Have defined or inherited foreground and background colors.
o Do NOT require horizontal scrolling when the text size is doubled.
webaim checks:
Blocks of text over one sentence in length:
o Are no more than 80 characters wide.
o Are NOT fully justified (aligned to both the left and the right margins).
o Have adequate line spacing (at least 1/2 the height of the text) and paragraph spacing (1.5 times line spacing).
o Have defined or inherited foreground and background colors.
o Do NOT require horizontal scrolling when the text size is doubled.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Images that appear to contain text are programmatically detected and flagged for review.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Images containing text are used only for decorative purposes and do not convey essential information.
When images of text convey information, the information cannot be presented using real text alone.
Decorative images of text are appropriately marked so they are ignored by assistive technologies.
Logos, branding, and other allowed exceptions are correctly identified and applied.
Total conditions: Images that appear to contain text are programmatically detected and flagged for review.
Images containing text are used only for decorative purposes and do not convey essential information.
When images of text convey information, the information cannot be presented using real text alone.
Decorative images of text are appropriately marked so they are ignored by assistive technologies.
Logos, branding, and other allowed exceptions are correctly identified and applied.
webaim checks:
Text is used within an image only for decoration (the image does not convey content) OR when the information
cannot be presented with text alone.

Remaining conditions required for full S: No loss of content or functionality occurs, and horizontal scrolling is avoided when content is presented at a width of 320 pixels.
This requires responsive design for most web sites.
This is best tested by setting the browser window to 1280 pixels wide and then zooming the page content to 400%.
Content that requires horizontal scrolling, such as data tables, complex images (such as maps and charts), toolbars, etc. are exempted.
Total conditions: No loss of content or functionality occurs, and horizontal scrolling is avoided when content is presented at a width of 320 pixels.
This requires responsive design for most web sites.
This is best tested by setting the browser window to 1280 pixels wide and then zooming the page content to 400%.
Content that requires horizontal scrolling, such as data tables, complex images (such as maps and charts), toolbars, etc. are exempted.
webaim checks:
No loss of content or functionality occurs, and horizontal scrolling is avoided when content is presented at a width of
320 pixels.
o This requires responsive design for most web sites. This is best tested by setting the browser window to 1280
pixels wide and then zooming the page content to 400%.
 Content that requires horizontal scrolling, such as data tables, complex images (such as maps and charts), toolbars,
etc. are exempted.

Remaining conditions required for full S: A contrast ratio of at least 3:1 is present for differentiating graphical objects (such as icons and components of charts or graphs) and author-customized interface components (such as buttons, form controls, and focus indicators/outlines).
At least 3:1 contrast is maintained in the various states (focus, hover, active, etc.) of author-customized interactive components.
Total conditions: A contrast ratio of at least 3:1 is present for differentiating graphical objects (such as icons and components of charts or graphs) and author-customized interface components (such as buttons, form controls, and focus indicators/outlines).
At least 3:1 contrast is maintained in the various states (focus, hover, active, etc.) of author-customized interactive components.
webaim checks:
A contrast ratio of at least 3:1 is present for differentiating graphical objects (such as icons and components of charts
or graphs) and author-customized interface components (such as buttons, form controls, and focus
indicators/outlines).
 At least 3:1 contrast is maintained in the various states (focus, hover, active, etc.) of author-customized interactive
components.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Inline styles do not set fixed line-height, letter-spacing, or word-spacing values that would prevent user text spacing adjustments.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Content remains readable and no text is clipped, overlapped, or truncated when paragraph, line, word, and letter spacing are increased to the specified values.
All functionality remains available and operable when text spacing is adjusted.
Fixed heights or containers do not cause loss of content when spacing is increased.
Text spacing adjustments do not require horizontal scrolling to read blocks of text.
Spacing adaptations work consistently across different browsers and assistive technologies.
Total conditions: Inline styles do not set fixed line-height, letter-spacing, or word-spacing values that would prevent user text spacing adjustments.
Content remains readable and no text is clipped, overlapped, or truncated when paragraph, line, word, and letter spacing are increased to the specified values.
All functionality remains available and operable when text spacing is adjusted.
Fixed heights or containers do not cause loss of content when spacing is increased.
Text spacing adjustments do not require horizontal scrolling to read blocks of text.
Spacing adaptations work consistently across different browsers and assistive technologies.
webaim checks:
No loss of content or functionality occurs when the user adapts paragraph spacing to 2 times the font size, text line
height/spacing to 1.5 times the font size, word spacing to .16 times the font size, and letter spacing to .12 times the
font size.
 This is best supported by avoiding pixel height definitions for elements that contain text.

Remaining conditions required for full S: When additional content is presented on hover or keyboard focus:

o The newly revealed content can be dismissed (generally via the Esc key) without moving the pointer or keyboard focus, unless the content presents an input error or does not obscure or interfere with other page content.
o The pointer can be moved to the new content without the content disappearing.
o The new content must remain visible until the pointer or keyboard focus is moved away from the triggering control, the new content is dismissed, or the new content is no longer relevant.
Total conditions: When additional content is presented on hover or keyboard focus: The newly revealed content can be dismissed (generally via the Esc key) without moving the pointer or keyboard focus, unless the content presents an input error or does not obscure or interfere with other page content.
When additional content is presented on hover or keyboard focus: The pointer can be moved to the new content without the content disappearing.

When additional content is presented on hover or keyboard focus: The new content must remain visible until the pointer or keyboard focus is moved away from the triggering control, the new content is dismissed, or the new content is no longer relevant.
webaim checks:
When additional content is presented on hover or keyboard focus:
o The newly revealed content can be dismissed (generally via the Esc key) without moving the pointer or keyboard
focus, unless the content presents an input error or does not obscure or interfere with other page content.
o The pointer can be moved to the new content without the content disappearing.
o The new content must remain visible until the pointer or keyboard focus is moved away from the triggering

automated checks (axe core rules ): Scrollable regions that contain keyboard-operable content are focusable using the keyboard.
All interactive elements and functionality on the page can be operated using the keyboard alone.
Remaining conditions required for full S: No functionality requires mouse-only, touch-only, or pointer-specific interactions.
Keyboard focus order allows users to reach and operate all interactive components.
Page-defined shortcut keys and accesskeys do not conflict with browser or assistive technology shortcuts.
Keyboard interactions are consistent and do not trap users within components.
Total conditions: Scrollable regions that contain keyboard-operable content are focusable using the keyboard.
All interactive elements and functionality on the page can be operated using the keyboard alone.
No functionality requires mouse-only, touch-only, or pointer-specific interactions.
Keyboard focus order allows users to reach and operate all interactive components.
Page-defined shortcut keys and accesskeys do not conflict with browser or assistive technology shortcuts.
Keyboard interactions are consistent and do not trap users within components.
webaim checks:
All page functionality is available using the keyboard, unless the functionality cannot be accomplished in any known
way using a keyboard (e.g., free hand drawing).
 Page-specified shortcut keys and accesskeys (accesskey should typically be avoided) do not conflict with existing
browser and screen reader shortcuts.

Remaining conditions required for full S: Keyboard focus is never locked or trapped at one particular page element.
The user can navigate to and from all navigable page elements using only a keyboard.
Total conditions: Keyboard focus is never locked or trapped at one particular page element.
The user can navigate to and from all navigable page elements using only a keyboard.
webaim checks:
Keyboard focus is never locked or trapped at one particular page element. The user can navigate to and from all
navigable page elements using only a keyboard.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Scrollable regions are keyboard focusable so users can scroll and interact with the content using only the keyboard.
Remaining conditions required for full S: All interactive functionality on the page can be operated using only the keyboard.
Keyboard users can access and operate custom widgets and components.
Keyboard focus order is logical and intuitive throughout the page.
Keyboard traps are not present and users can move focus away from all components.
All keyboard interactions work consistently across browsers and assistive technologies.
Time-based or gesture-based interactions have equivalent keyboard alternatives.
Total conditions: Scrollable regions are keyboard focusable so users can scroll and interact with the content using only the keyboard.
All interactive functionality on the page can be operated using only the keyboard.
Keyboard users can access and operate custom widgets and components.
Keyboard focus order is logical and intuitive throughout the page.
Keyboard traps are not present and users can move focus away from all components.
All keyboard interactions work consistently across browsers and assistive technologies.
Time-based or gesture-based interactions have equivalent keyboard alternatives.
webaim checks: All page functionality is available using the keyboard.

Remaining conditions required for full S: If a keyboard shortcut uses printable character keys, then the user must be able to disable the key command, change the defined key to a non-printable key (Ctrl, Alt, etc.), or only activate the shortcut when an associated interface component or button is focused.
Total conditions: If a keyboard shortcut uses printable character keys, then the user must be able to disable the key command, change the defined key to a non-printable key (Ctrl, Alt, etc.), or only activate the shortcut when an associated interface component or button is focused.
webaim checks:
If a keyboard shortcut uses printable character keys, then the user must be able to disable the key command, change
the defined key to a non-printable key (Ctrl, Alt, etc.), or only activate the shortcut when an associated interface
component or button is focused.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Pages do not use automatic meta refresh mechanisms that refresh or redirect the page without user control.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Time limits imposed by scripts, sessions, or applications provide a user-controlled mechanism to turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit.
Users are warned before a time limit expires and given sufficient opportunity to extend it.
Time limit controls are accessible using the keyboard and assistive technologies.
Exceptions for real-time events are correctly applied.
Time limits longer than 20 hours are correctly identified and excluded from this requirement.
Total conditions: Pages do not use automatic meta refresh mechanisms that refresh or redirect the page without user control.
Time limits imposed by scripts, sessions, or applications provide a user-controlled mechanism to turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit.
Users are warned before a time limit expires and given sufficient opportunity to extend it.
Time limit controls are accessible using the keyboard and assistive technologies.
Exceptions for real-time events are correctly applied.
Time limits longer than 20 hours are correctly identified and excluded from this requirement.
webaim checks:
If a page or application has a time limit, the user is given options to turn off, adjust, or extend that time limit. This is
not a requirement for real-time events (e.g., an auction), where the time limit is absolutely required, or if the time
limit is longer than 20 hours.

automated checks (axe core rules ): Blinking content created using deprecated HTML elements (such as <blink>) is not present.
Remaining conditions required for full S: Automatically moving or scrolling content (e.g., carousels, sliders, marquees, animations) provides a user-controlled mechanism to pause, stop, or hide the movement.
Automatically updating content (e.g., news tickers, live updates, chat feeds) can be paused, stopped, hidden, or controlled by the user.
Controls to pause, stop, or hide moving or updating content are clearly visible and accessible.
Pause and control mechanisms are keyboard accessible.
Moving or updating content does not resume automatically without user initiation.
Total conditions: Blinking content created using deprecated HTML elements (such as <blink>) is not present.
Automatically moving or scrolling content (e.g., carousels, sliders, marquees, animations) provides a user-controlled mechanism to pause, stop, or hide the movement.
Automatically updating content (e.g., news tickers, live updates, chat feeds) can be paused, stopped, hidden, or controlled by the user.
Controls to pause, stop, or hide moving or updating content are clearly visible and accessible.
Pause and control mechanisms are keyboard accessible.
